en.name: Leo X
en.summary: A lavish Medici patron of the arts whose sale of indulgences to fund St. Peter's Basilica helped provoke Martin Luther's revolt.
en.body: Giovanni de' Medici brought Florentine extravagance to the papal court, spending freely on art, music, and entertainment, reportedly remarking, "God has given us the papacy, let us enjoy it." His expansion of indulgence sales to help finance the rebuilding of St. Peter's Basilica became a flashpoint for Martin Luther's Ninety-Five Theses in 1517, and Leo's 1521 bull excommunicating Luther marked the point of no return for the Reformation his own financial policies had helped ignite.
